subject.title: [Feature]: Support for Custom Emojis in Latest Telegram Bot API Update

question: What public API shape should OpenClaw expose for Telegram custom emoji entities in shared message-tool sends, captions, edits, and replies?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but adding raw entities, Telegram-specific channel data, or a portable custom-emoji span changes the public message-tool/plugin boundary and fallback semantics.

options.title: Define entity-bearing message API
options.body: Add a maintainer-approved entity representation and implement it consistently across message-tool, Telegram send/edit/caption/reply delivery, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep rich HTML and richMessages only
options.body: Treat `<tg-emoji>` HTML and opt-in Bot API rich messages as the supported path while leaving user-supplied entity arrays unsupported.

options.title: Split API design first
options.body: Create or designate a narrower API-design item before implementation so the eventual PR does not guess the permanent plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Define entity-bearing message API
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-approved entity representation and implement it consistently across message-tool, Telegram send/edit/caption/reply delivery, docs, and regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is already the strongest issue-thread and Telegram formatting/API-shape routing signal for this specific decision.
